Synopsis:
    Weekly jobless claims edged up 2K to 206K (week ending Aug 29), staying near the lower end of the 2026 range. The labor market remains in "slow hire, slow fire" mode — layoffs are historically low but hiring is sluggish. Continuing claims rose slightly to 1.779M. Friday's NFP print is expected to show a +56K rebound after July's -23K, though a second consecutive month of job losses cannot be ruled out given Haitian TPS expiry. The Fed, under Chairman Kevin Warsh, is expected to raise rates as early as September to fight tariff- and war-driven inflation, with Warsh signaling more tightening ahead if inflation doesn't converge to 2%.

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +70 (Meaningfully more hawkish) — The most current signals are unambiguous: Warsh explicitly flagged "work to do" if inflation doesn't fall, a September hike is the base case, and inflation is being driven by structural forces (tariffs, geopolitical war) rather than demand overheating — making a dovish pivot unlikely near-term. Labor market resilience (low layoffs) removes urgency to ease.
